Subject: Dedicated capacity — multi-region standby options and cost model

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. We liked the idea of a hot primary in us-west with a cold standby in eu-west for DR. Before we get legal involved we need a clearer commercial model for:

- Separate reserved pools per region vs a single pooled commit with cross-region failover charges
- Pricing for active mirroring (both pools live) vs standby (pay lower reserve until failover)
- Throughput guarantees: how you size a pool for our 600 rps steady, 1.2k burst and what that maps to in GPU slots

Can you provide a written sketch (numbers) and any tradeoffs on credits/discounts if we commit 18 months? Procurement pushed that term. Also, any standard crediting approach when failover is invoked (SLA credits vs ephemeral burst allowances)?

Jordan — thanks for the clear asks. High level sketch below; attaching a spreadsheet with ballpark numbers (RWD_dedicated_pricing_sketch_v2.xlsx).

1) Topology options
a) Dual-active (us-west + eu-west both reserved): higher steady cost, zero cross-region warmup; recommended if you need RPO ~0 and <200ms cross-region failover for sessions.
b) Active + cold-standby (reserve smaller standby footprint and rapid scale-on-failover): lower committed cost, slightly longer warmup (we ship pre-warmed images to reduce cold start).

2) Sizing guidance for your profile (600 rps steady, 1.2k burst) — rough math
- Our GPU slot sizing: 1 "slot" ~= 250 rps for model family X-2Q @ typical prompt mix.
- Steady 600 rps => 3 slots; burst headroom to 1.2k => plan 5 slots (3 active + 2 burst).
- Each slot priced in the sketch with reserved-rate and on-demand burst rate.

3) Commit & discount framing (18 months)
- Base reserved discount: 25% off hosted rates for single-region 18mo commit.
- Dual-region committed (separate pools): incremental 12% cross-region bundle discount applied to second-region reserves.
- If you commit to active-active across both regions we can add a further 5% enterprise overlay (requires minimum 6 slots total).

4) Failover credits / SLA treatment
- If standby is passive and you trigger DR we provide a one-time credit equal to 30% of the standby monthly commit for the month of failover + 72 hours of sustained burst backfill credits.
- For active-active failures we follow standard SLA credits (per SLA table) based on observed downtime.

Next steps: I'll loop in Rishi (pricing) and Kim (legal commercial) to firm numbers. If this looks directionally right, we can produce a clean commercial term sheet and a draft MSA for procurement.

Best,
Mina

Subject: Fwd: pricing sketch + carve-outs for standby credits

Mina / Kim — quick internal: Jordan asked specifically about credits when failover is invoked. My recommended negotiation points:

- For active+standby, offer the 30% one-time failover credit but cap to one invocation per 12 months unless there is systemic platform outage. That prevents repeated test failovers from being expensive.
- Instead of a pure standby reserve fraction, propose a "warm reserve" SKU: 40% of full slot cost but with guaranteed <10m scale-up SLA. Bill as reserved but at 40% price to reflect reduced capacity. This makes accounting simpler for procurement.
- For throughput guarantees, avoid per-rps SLOs; commit to slot counts and 99.9% throughput availability for allocated slots. Use our token-level tracing to show tail latency.

Discount levers to propose:
- 18mo commit: base 28% instead of 25% if they sign by EoQ and agree to bundled billing across regions.
- Cross-region bundle: additional 10% off second-region reserves (structured as a stacking discount).
- Capability credits: waive first-month standby charge for the cold standby if they accept a 6+ slot minimum.

Kim — any legal concerns with capping failover credits? If ok we can make the term sheet and present.

-Rishi
